trajectory_summary: The call opens efficiently with a low-friction, appointment-already-exists framing that gets the customer engaged fast, and the rep runs the tax/credit qualifier cleanly. But the call disintegrates in the back half: the customer surfaces real scheduling chaos (no scheduler, no computer, needs a callback after 3PM tomorrow) and the rep responds with a vague 'callback or text' offer instead of locking the specific window the customer just gave, ending in an unconfirmed 40-minute phone-call proposal that the customer never explicitly accepts before hanging up.
outcome_dispute: This should not be read as a clean 'callback' or 'tentative' outcome. No day or time was locked — the customer named 'after 3PM tomorrow' as their availability at 02:27, but the rep never repeated it back or confirmed it, and the call ends with the customer saying 'I gotta go' before agreeing to the rep's 40-minute-call proposal. This is closer to an unanchored soft exit than a real booked callback.
